title: Sub-Scope Publishing
summary: coordinate optional document subjects, folder-state reconciliation, catalogue-document reporting, current references, editorial copy and public reverse links
content_html:
Sub-Scope Publishing

Purpose

Sub-Scope Publishing coordinates the path from private working documents to maintained contextual references and reviewed public documents. All normal working documents may remain together in dotlineform/projects and optionally declare folder_path, work_id, series_id, or no subject. Focused projections then support Manage authoring cues, Project State, catalogue-document coverage reporting, current-reference rendering, editorial copy, and public catalogue metadata without making subject presence a lifecycle gate.

The feature keeps one sequence because subject declaration, reverse association, Project State, Resolver Tokens, collection-aware copy, and Work/Series-page document links share one authoring-to-publication foundation. Project State remains folder-specific, while Work/Series reverse association is optional document metadata that may participate from any public collection.

SSC-1 — Unified Sub-Scope Customisation Contract Delivery is the shared configuration prerequisite. It establishes one registered sub_scope_customisation seam for report projections, read-only metadata, focused actions, validation, import, and transfer aspects before SSP adds a Projects assignable-subject group. SSP does not create a parallel declared-fields workflow.

SSP-0 — Projects Subject Assignment Foundation Delivery is the completed standalone prerequisite to subject implementation. It keeps Info read-only, moves Projects folder assignment from Edit metadata into a modal selected by the sub-scope's declared assignment capability, and establishes the exact-target mutation and interaction seams that SSP-1 extends with Work/Series search. Projects is the current configuration registrant, not a hard-coded browser condition.

SSP-1 — Document Subject And Association Delivery is complete. SSP-2 — Docs Viewer Project State Delivery is the current delivery. Its SSP-2.0 sanity note records the accepted implementation fit, direct-project-folder boundary, scan timing, risks, and review gate; work remains stopped before SSP-2.1 approval.

Sub-Scope Publishing Concept And Architecture owns the complete cross-delivery model. All retained concept, architecture, and delivery documents are direct children of this feature. Delivery titles use SSP numbering, so the index tree expresses a possible implementation order without a separately maintained order table.

Complete Feature Outcome

A working document in dotlineform/projects may declare zero or one of normalized folder_path, canonical work_id, and canonical series_id. This is an authoring convention rather than a save, Copy, viewability, or Publish requirement. Valid declarations project deterministic zero-to-many document associations without inferring identity from title, filename, body content, route state, destination, or current UI context. Malformed or conflicting declarations remain non-blocking authoring evidence and do not enter reverse lookups.

Project State consumes only valid folder declarations from the shared working collection, plus immediate project-directory inventory and canonical Work/Series evidence. Matching works[] remain explicit by canonical identity and current series_ids, while catalogue status retains its existing catalogue owner; series[] supplies grouping context and per-Series Work counts. Work-subject, Series-subject, and no-subject documents coexist without entering the folder report. A context-aware Resolver Token renders the exact current folder, Work, Series, or document references for its containing document without serializing the subject in token source or refreshing relationship data.

The Work/Series-to-document associations also satisfy a curator reporting requirement: Studio must be able to show catalogue document coverage by exact Work or Series and open the associated documents. The current Catalogue Works index is the likely presentation family, while its eventual route and component shape may be chosen as part of a later Studio Works refactor. The reporting view consumes the shared derived associations rather than introducing another working collection or relationship authority.

Collection-aware copy takes a dotlineform/projects document into the exact analysis/works collection as an independent non-viewable editorial copy. Shared work_id or series_id metadata is retained; unsupported folder_path is omitted and reported; a no-subject document copies normally. Later private-source changes do not retarget the independent copy. Ordinary publication remains subject-agnostic, while exact public Work or Series by-ID payloads receive deterministic derived doc_url[] values from any published document whose final source has a valid matching declaration.

Boundary

Sub-Scope Publishing owns the cross-feature goal, SSP delivery sequence, shared typed-subject contract, and handoffs between working, derived, editorial, and public projections. The flat child documents own their exact schemas, builders, UI, reports, registries, tests, and review gates.

The feature does not make document titles or content into identity, impose one-to-one subject cardinality, make subject metadata a publication rule, synchronize document lifecycle with folders, Works, or Series, infer a catalogue subject from a Project folder, roll Work associations up to Series or Series associations down to member Works, let Resolver Tokens refresh relationship data, publish Manage-only paths, or make copy and publication one mutation. It does not prohibit a later general relationship database for analysis; such a store does not replace explicit source authorities or focused consumer projections.

Semantic Tokens remains the link and usage owner for returned registered identities. The existing Analysis Publish workflow remains the only public publication authority.

Delivery Discipline

The feature-level sense check is complete. Delivery .0 steps confirm implementation fit, current broad owners, shared-customisation prerequisites, and stop conditions; they do not reopen the one-working-collection, optional-subject, subject-independent publication, or folder-to-Work Project State decisions.

Each SSP delivery begins with a short scope-and-spec sanity gate. That gate confirms scheduling dependencies, the fit with current broad owners, the likely blast radius, the intended deliverables, principal risks, and a concrete stop condition. It resolves only contradictions that would change the specified outcome; it does not require an exhaustive code audit, exact file inventory, line estimate, frozen implementation, implemented fixture, or complete test architecture before implementation approval.

Each implementation step remains independently reviewable. Before proceeding to the next step, focused evidence must prove the changed contract and an independent code/diff review must check scope, ownership, omissions, surviving boundaries, and whether the delivery documents remain accurate. The final transfer step retains the broader completion, documentation, and omission review.
